text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.4% today as oil prices dropped on geopolitical easing in the Middle East. Iran signaled willingness to return to nuclear talks and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which reduced immediate concerns about supply disruptions that had been supporting crude prices—US oil fell from recent highs as traders priced in lower conflict risk. The stock has now lost 2.6% over two weeks, tracking the decline from $424.89 on September 18th.

The timing matters because refiners like Marathon profit most when crude prices are elevated and stable. While refineries are running at a healthy 94% capacity and diesel inventory is relatively tight at 107 million barrels, the easing of Iran tensions removed one of the few near-term props holding oil prices up. The broader risk—a potential diesel export ban—would actually squeeze the refining business long-term, so geopolitical de-escalation that might seem good for consumers is mixed news for a refiner's margins.
